summary: Retroactive reserved-hours reallocation caused credit hold and autopay failure for Acme Analytics
description:
Issue summary: Acme Analytics reports that a mid-cycle reallocation of reserved GPU hours (admin-initiated reparenting of subaccounts) resulted in a portion of their provisional credits being moved to an archived cost center. The migration triggered a credit hold which caused autopay to fail on their most recent invoice.

Impact: Customer autopay failed for the current billing cycle, leaving a negative provisional balance and a blocked reserved-hours payout. Customer workspace experienced billing alerts and delayed capacity adjustments (they temporarily lost burst credits for several reserved workloads).

Customer quote (from support email): 'We saw a -$2,130 provisional balance and autopay declined even though we had enough reserve credits. Our reserved hours were reallocated between subaccounts last night; now invoices show credits stuck under an "archived-cost-center" and autopay is not picking them up.'
timeline:
2026-03-12 02:15 UTC - Customer requests help reporting negative provisional balance.
2026-03-12 03:05 UTC - Support triages and confirms credit movement to archived cost center tag.
2026-03-12 04:40 UTC - Billing team confirms reserved-hours reallocation job ran at 2026-03-11T23:59:12Z.
2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Finance request to hold autopay until root cause investigation.
2026-03-14 11:30 UTC - Engineering identified postback re-mapping bug in reparenting flow (PR opened).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Admin reparent subaccount B into parent Org A via org-migration API.
2) Reserved-hours reallocation job executes (batch reassign).
3) Postback reconciler processes hourly credit assignment and tags cost center.
4) Archived cost center tag is incorrectly applied when the original subaccount had an archived flag.
5) Finance/autopay pipeline excludes archived cost centers from automatic debit, causing autopay to fail.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Reparenting job copied an 'archived' flag from an old subaccount record into the cost center tag used by postback reconciler, causing autopay to exclude credits.
Hypothesis 2: Hourly postback ordering race where reallocation job completed after the postback snapshot, leaving credits orphaned under an outdated cost center mapping.
Partial finding: Logs show explicit WARN for cost_center=archived-cost-center and autopay skip_charge triggered the same minute; correlates with reallocation job timestamp.
Correlation: Customer performed manual subaccount reparent at 2026-03-11 23:58 UTC; reallocation batch window includes that timestamp.
Related bug: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2789 shows code diff to ignore archived flag in cost center mapping.
resolution: In Progress - temporary mitigation applied: Finance placed autopay on manual hold while Engineering prepares a one-time credit reallocation script. Engineering PR #2789 created to fix archived flag propagation. Pending final finance approval for automated ledger correction and customer confirmation to re-enable autopay.
next_steps: Engineering: Finish and deploy PR #2789 to staging and run the reserved-hours reallocation job in dry-run mode (owner: Luca, target: 2026-03-15).
Finance: Approve one-time ledger transfer to move $2,130 from archived-cost-center to acct-acme parent cost center and clear negative provisional balance (owner: Tomás, ETA: 2026-03-15).
Support: Coordinate with customer to confirm post-fix invoice and re-enable autopay once ledger fix confirmed (owner: Maya, contact: Priya Rao).
Follow-up: Create postmortem runbook for org reparenting reserved-hour reallocation and add regression tests covering archived flags in cost center mapping.
